report.summary: As of 2026-10-12 12:00 UTC, RR-001 is in prelaunch preparation for an approved 2,000-account cohort targeted for 2026-10-16 10:00 UTC. Support is not ready: cancellation training and draft public guidance conflict with approved v2, KI-17 guidance lacks Sam's approval and availability, public content is unpublished, CRM reasons are not deployed to both forms, vendor enablement and staffing acceptance are pending, and the scheduled announcement provides only 48 of the required 72 hours. If ANN-1 retains its 2026-10-14 10:00 UTC schedule, the launch target must move to at least 2026-10-17 10:00 UTC. No launch authorization, customer exposure, observed rollout telemetry, or pause condition is established.

findings.finding: The affected cancellation guidance conflicts with approved v2. The draft public article treats clicking Cancel subscription as completion, while training tells agents that the button completes cancellation, to refresh Billing, and to assure customers another charge will not happen. Approved v2 requires review and confirmation, completion only after billing acknowledgement, and says refreshing is not a billing guarantee. Twelve internal agents already attended training based on the older proposal.
findings.customer_consequence: Agents or customers could falsely conclude that cancellation completed or that no future charge can occur before billing confirms the action.
findings.proposed_action: Ren must revise the affected public and internal cancellation guidance to match v2. Nia must replace the affected training, correct the 12 pilot attendees, and record current coverage before exposure. Retain the unchanged reminder and refund-review guidance.

evidence.quote: Product documents define approved intended behavior. Test records are evidence of simulated checks, not proof of every possible outcome. A help article or training slide cannot override approved behavior. If a later approved change affects guidance, review that guidance again. Earlier records remain historical evidence. Plans and drafts are not completed actions; an owner name is not an approval.

Cancellation and billing guidance must match the approved flow. Public content must be published for the exposed cohort. Every known billing issue needs safe guidance, an escalation route and the product owner's acceptance before exposure. Support launch readiness is not ready if this evidence is missing or contradicts the current behavior.

Manage Plan → Cancel subscription → review paid-access end date → Confirm cancellation. Show completion only after billing acknowledges it. Keep paid access until term end; stop future renewals after confirmed cancellation. Do not say access ends immediately. A pending request or a click alone is not confirmation.

On slow responses the invoice page can display a stale renewal date for up to ten minutes after confirmed cancellation. Dev's simulated test T-17 confirms this display issue; it does not establish that a specific customer's charge is valid. Support must confirm the billing cancellation record, explain the display delay and escalate any actual post-cancellation charge to Sam. Refreshing the page is not a guarantee that billing is correct.
Owners: Ren (content), Nia (training). Updated: 2026-10-11 09:00 UTC. Based on product proposal v1. Status: draft.

Open Manage Plan and click Cancel subscription. Your cancellation is complete and there will be no further renewals. You keep access to the end of your paid term. Cancelling does not refund that term; a person must review refund requests.

The cancellation button completes cancellation. Ask the customer to refresh Billing to see the new date. If the date is unchanged, reassure them that another charge will not happen. Refunds require billing review; do not promise one.
